instagram.caption:
Claim your business in ChatGPT, and you agree not to sue OpenAI over what you publish on your site.
That is in OpenAI's terms for businesses, with one exception: a claim that OpenAI broke those terms. You also agree its AI assistant may call your business for its users (you can opt out).
OpenAI calls the place Business Hub, and it's in beta. Four steps to claim:
1. Open Business Hub: chatgpt.com/business-hub
2. Search your business name. The line under the search box says: "By continuing, you accept OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT Terms."
3. Prove it's yours with a method OpenAI offers you, such as your business phone, a business email or your website domain.
4. Pass an identity check before any change goes live.
The catch: OpenAI's help page says local stores and restaurants can only claim a listing that already exists, and only a U.S. listing, for now.
Our call, and we're not lawyers: OpenAI's terms say it may list a business whether the owner claims it or not. Already listed, and want your info kept current? Claim it, then opt out of the calls. If you sell what's on your website, read the terms first. The terms also say claiming does not give you exclusive control of the listing. OpenAI says claiming doesn't guarantee ChatGPT recommends you more.
Would you sign that to claim your listing?
Save this, and send it to whoever handles your listings online.
Source: OpenAI, "Businesses in ChatGPT Terms" (last updated Nov 9, 2026); OpenAI, "Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT" (Nov 10, 2026); OpenAI Help Center, "Setting up your business on ChatGPT". All read Nov 12, 2026. The Business Hub screens are from our own account.
